title.en: Finding Your Human Voice in the Age of AI

narrative_brief: Mini PechaKucha for Science Communication (SDG 9 × AI Literacy × Science Communication)

A2.text: Good morning. Today we look at SDG 9, a world plan from the United Nations. It helps every country build better factories and support modern science.
A2.authored_by: Claude (English teacher role), v2 against the v2 quality gate
A2.basis: Full rewrite. The earlier overlay still failed eight of twelve slides and soft-missed three quarters of them, mostly by running under the 20-second fill floor and below the A2 Flesch-Kincaid band, and several slides repeated the B1 wording almost word for word. This text is written from the source meaning in present-simple spoken English, one idea per sentence, with a because-clause on slide 5 and a before-clause on slide 9 so the A2 grammar is visible, and no participle clauses, clefts or fronting. Meaning, slide order and every named fact are unchanged: SDG 9, the United Nations, ChatGPT, Gemini, AI slop, the four parts of a prompt (role, background, goal, limit). Facts corrected: the workbook says the model 'only guesses the next word' and 'does not understand your ideas'. A language model predicts the next word, and it works only from the words in the prompt plus the patterns in its training text, so slide 5 says it never reads your mind and only sees the words you type. Slide 12 ends on the claim: the workbook's 'Thank you' was cut, because it kills the applause line.

B1.authored_by: Claude (English teacher role), v2 against the v2 quality gate
B1.basis: Full rewrite. The workbook B1 column failed ten of twelve slides - semicolons and em-dashes that give a speaker no breathing cue, sentences of thirty words or more, and a long-word share at B2 level - and it sat 0.52 from the B2 text, which means the two levels were one text.
